passages.text: On that day Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sang this song: “When the princes take the lead in Israel, when the people volunteer, bless the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Deborah was a prophetess and a leader in Israel.
Barak was the son of Abinoam.
On that day, Deborah and Barak sang a song.
They said these words.
When the leaders in Israel take charge, good things happen.
When the people offer themselves willingly, God is pleased.
Bless the LORD.
passages.original: וַתָּ֣שַׁר דְּבוֹרָ֔ה וּבָרָ֖ק בֶּן־ אֲבִינֹ֑עַם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא לֵאמֹֽר׃ בִּפְרֹ֤עַ פְּרָעוֹת֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּהִתְנַדֵּ֖ב עָ֑ם בָּרֲכ֖וּ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Listen, O kings! Give ear, O princes! I will sing to the LORD; I will sing praise to the LORD, the God of Israel.
passages.sermon:
Deborah was a prophetess and a leader in Israel.
Barak was the son of Abinoam.
On that day, Deborah and Barak sang a song.
They spoke to all rulers and leaders.
Listen, kings.
Pay attention, princes.
I will sing to the LORD.
I will praise the LORD, the God of Israel.
passages.original: שִׁמְע֣וּ מְלָכִ֔ים הַאֲזִ֖ינוּ רֹֽזְנִ֑ים אָֽנֹכִ֗י לַֽיהוָה֙ אָנֹכִ֣י אָשִׁ֔ירָה אֲזַמֵּ֕ר לַֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: O LORD, when You went out from Seir, when You marched from the land of Edom, the earth trembled, the heavens poured out rain, and the clouds poured down water.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD went out from Seir.
The LORD marched from the land of Edom.
The earth trembled.
The heavens poured out rain.
The clouds poured down water.
passages.original: יְהוָ֗ה בְּצֵאתְךָ֤ מִשֵּׂעִיר֙ בְּצַעְדְּךָ֙ מִשְּׂדֵ֣ה אֱד֔וֹם אֶ֣רֶץ רָעָ֔שָׁה גַּם־ שָׁמַ֖יִם נָטָ֑פוּ גַּם־ עָבִ֖ים נָ֥טְפוּ מָֽיִם׃

passages.text: The mountains quaked before the LORD, the One of Sinai, before the LORD, the God of Israel.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD came from Sinai.
The mountains shook before the LORD.
The mountains trembled before the God of Israel.
passages.original: הָרִ֥ים נָזְל֖וּ מִפְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה זֶ֣ה סִינַ֔י מִפְּנֵ֕י יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the highways were deserted and the travelers took the byways.
passages.sermon:
Shamgar was the son of Anath.
Jael was a woman in Israel.
These events happened during their days.
The highways became empty.
No one traveled on the main roads.
Travelers used winding byways instead.
passages.original: בִּימֵ֞י שַׁמְגַּ֤ר בֶּן־ עֲנָת֙ בִּימֵ֣י יָעֵ֔ל חָדְל֖וּ אֳרָח֑וֹת וְהֹלְכֵ֣י נְתִיב֔וֹת יֵלְכ֕וּ אֳרָח֖וֹת עֲקַלְקַלּֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Life in the villages ceased; it ended in Israel, until I, Deborah, arose, a mother in Israel.
passages.sermon:
Life in the villages stopped in Israel.
No one lived freely in the open country.
This continued for a long time.
Then I, Deborah, stood up.
I became a leader in Israel.
I became a mother to Israel.
passages.original: חָדְל֧וּ פְרָז֛וֹן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל חָדֵ֑לּוּ עַ֤ד שַׁקַּ֙מְתִּי֙ דְּבוֹרָ֔ה שַׁקַּ֥מְתִּי אֵ֖ם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: When they chose new gods, then war came to their gates. Not a shield or spear was found among forty thousand in Israel.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel chose new gods.
War came to their city gates.
Israel had forty thousand people.
No one in Israel had a shield.
No one in Israel had a spear.
passages.original: יִבְחַר֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים חֲדָשִׁ֔ים אָ֖ז לָחֶ֣ם שְׁעָרִ֑ים מָגֵ֤ן אִם־ יֵֽרָאֶה֙ וָרֹ֔מַח בְּאַרְבָּעִ֥ים אֶ֖לֶף בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: My heart is with the princes of Israel, with the volunteers among the people. Bless the LORD!
passages.sermon:
Deborah speaks as a leader and prophetess in Israel.
She says her heart is with the princes of Israel.
These princes are the leaders of the people.
Her heart is also with the volunteers among the people.
These volunteers willingly offered themselves to help.
She calls everyone to bless the LORD.
passages.original: לִבִּי֙ לְחוֹקְקֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַמִּֽתְנַדְּבִ֖ים בָּעָ֑ם בָּרֲכ֖וּ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: You who ride white donkeys, who sit on saddle blankets, and you who travel the road, ponder the voices of the singers at the watering places. There they shall recount the righteous acts of the LORD, the righteous deeds of His villagers in Israel. Then the people of the LORD went down to the gates: ‘Awake, awake, O Deborah! Awake, awake, sing a song! Arise, O Barak, and take hold of your captives, O son of Abinoam!’
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel had leaders and volunteers.
Some people rode white donkeys.
Some people sat on saddle blankets.
Some people traveled on the road.
All these people should listen.
They should listen to the voices at the watering places.
At the watering places, singers raised their voices.
There, the singers told about the LORD’s righteous acts.
They spoke about the righteous deeds of the LORD’s villagers in Israel.
After this, the people of the LORD went down to the city gates.
A call went out to Deborah.
The call said, “Awake, awake, Deborah!”
“Awake, awake, speak a song!”
A call went out to Barak, son of Abinoam.
The call said, “Arise, Barak!”
“Take hold of your captives!”
passages.original: רֹכְבֵי֩ אֲתֹנ֨וֹת צְחֹר֜וֹת יֹשְׁבֵ֧י עַל־ מִדִּ֛ין וְהֹלְכֵ֥י עַל־ דֶּ֖רֶךְ שִֽׂיחוּ׃ מִקּ֣וֹל מְחַֽצְצִ֗ים בֵּ֚ין מַשְׁאַבִּ֔ים שָׁ֤ם יְתַנּוּ֙ צִדְק֣וֹת יְהוָ֔ה צִדְקֹ֥ת פִּרְזֹנ֖וֹ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אָ֛ז יָרְד֥וּ לַשְּׁעָרִ֖ים עַם־ יְהוָֽה׃ עוּרִ֤י עוּרִי֙ דְּבוֹרָ֔ה ע֥וּרִי ע֖וּרִי דַּבְּרִי־ שִׁ֑יר ק֥וּם בָּרָ֛ק וּֽשֲׁבֵ֥ה שֶׁבְיְךָ֖ בֶּן־ אֲבִינֹֽעַם׃

passages.text: Then the survivors came down to the nobles; the people of the LORD came down to me against the mighty.
passages.sermon: The survivors came down to the nobles.\r\nThe people of the LORD came down to me.\r\nThey came against the mighty.
passages.original: אָ֚ז יְרַ֣ד שָׂרִ֔יד לְאַדִּירִ֖ים עָ֑ם יְהוָ֕ה יְרַד־ לִ֖י בַּגִּבּוֹרִֽים׃

passages.text: Some came from Ephraim, with their roots in Amalek; Benjamin came with your people after you. The commanders came down from Machir, the bearers of the marshal’s staff from Zebulun.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel gathered for battle.
Some people came from Ephraim.
Their ancestors had lived among the Amalekites.
Benjamin followed after you with your people.
Commanders came down from Machir.
Leaders came from Zebulun.
They carried the staff of a scribe.
passages.original: מִנִּ֣י אֶפְרַ֗יִם שָׁרְשָׁם֙ בַּעֲמָלֵ֔ק אַחֲרֶ֥יךָ בִנְיָמִ֖ין בַּֽעֲמָמֶ֑יךָ מִנִּ֣י מָכִ֗יר יָֽרְדוּ֙ מְחֹ֣קְקִ֔ים וּמִ֨זְּבוּלֻ֔ן מֹשְׁכִ֖ים בְּשֵׁ֥בֶט סֹפֵֽר׃

passages.text: The princes of Issachar were with Deborah, and Issachar was with Barak, rushing into the valley at his heels. In the clans of Reuben there was great indecision.
passages.sermon:
The princes of Issachar joined Deborah.
Issachar also followed Barak.
Barak led them into the valley.
They hurried after him.
The clans of Reuben felt great indecision.
passages.original: וְשָׂרַ֤י בְּיִשָּׂשכָר֙ עִם־ דְּבֹרָ֔ה וְיִשָּׂשכָר֙ כֵּ֣ן בָּרָ֔ק בָּעֵ֖מֶק שֻׁלַּ֣ח בְּרַגְלָ֑יו בִּפְלַגּ֣וֹת רְאוּבֵ֔ן גְּדֹלִ֖ים חִקְקֵי־ לֵֽב׃

passages.text: Why did you sit among the sheepfolds to hear the whistling for the flocks? In the clans of Reuben there was great indecision.
passages.sermon:
The tribe of Reuben had great indecision.
You sat among the sheepfolds.
You listened to the whistling for the flocks.
You did not act.
You hesitated when action was needed.
passages.original: לָ֣מָּה יָשַׁ֗בְתָּ בֵּ֚ין הַֽמִּשְׁפְּתַ֔יִם לִשְׁמֹ֖עַ שְׁרִק֣וֹת עֲדָרִ֑ים לִפְלַגּ֣וֹת רְאוּבֵ֔ן גְּדוֹלִ֖ים חִקְרֵי־ לֵֽב׃

passages.text: Gilead remained beyond the Jordan. Dan, why did you linger by the ships? Asher stayed at the coast and remained in his harbors.
passages.sermon:
Gilead stayed east of the Jordan River.
Dan stayed near the ships.
Asher lived by the seashore.
Asher remained in his harbors.
passages.original: גִּלְעָ֗ד בְּעֵ֤בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ שָׁכֵ֔ן וְדָ֕ן לָ֥מָּה יָג֖וּר אֳנִיּ֑וֹת אָשֵׁ֗ר יָשַׁב֙ לְח֣וֹף יַמִּ֔ים וְעַ֥ל מִפְרָצָ֖יו יִשְׁכּֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Zebulun was a people who risked their lives; Naphtali, too, on the heights of the battlefield.
passages.sermon:
Zebulun was a tribe of Israel.
Zebulun risked their lives in battle.
Naphtali was also a tribe of Israel.
Naphtali fought on the heights of the battlefield.
Both Zebulun and Naphtali showed courage.
passages.original: זְבֻל֗וּן עַ֣ם חֵרֵ֥ף נַפְשׁ֛וֹ לָמ֖וּת וְנַפְתָּלִ֑י עַ֖ל מְרוֹמֵ֥י שָׂדֶֽה׃

passages.text: Kings came and fought; then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo, but they took no plunder of silver.
passages.sermon:
Kings came.
They fought.
The kings of Canaan fought.
They fought at Taanach.
They fought by the waters of Megiddo.
They did not take any silver as plunder.
passages.original: בָּ֤אוּ מְלָכִים֙ נִלְחָ֔מוּ אָ֤ז נִלְחֲמוּ֙ מַלְכֵ֣י כְנַ֔עַן בְּתַעְנַ֖ךְ עַל־ מֵ֣י מְגִדּ֑וֹ בֶּ֥צַע כֶּ֖סֶף לֹ֥א לָקָֽחוּ׃

passages.text: From the heavens the stars fought; from their courses they fought against Sisera.
passages.sermon: The stars fought from the heavens.\r\nThey fought from their courses.\r\nThey fought against Sisera.
passages.original: מִן־ שָׁמַ֖יִם נִלְחָ֑מוּ הַכּֽוֹכָבִים֙ מִמְּסִלּוֹתָ֔ם נִלְחֲמ֖וּ עִם־ סִיסְרָֽא׃

passages.text: The River Kishon swept them away, the ancient river, the River Kishon. March on, O my soul, in strength!
passages.sermon:
The River Kishon swept them away.
This river is ancient.
The River Kishon did this.
My soul, go forward in strength.
passages.original: נַ֤חַל קִישׁוֹן֙ גְּרָפָ֔ם נַ֥חַל קְדוּמִ֖ים נַ֣חַל קִישׁ֑וֹן תִּדְרְכִ֥י נַפְשִׁ֖י עֹֽז׃

passages.text: Then the hooves of horses thundered— the mad galloping of his stallions.
passages.sermon:
The horses ran fast.
Their hooves thundered on the ground.
The stallions galloped wildly.
The sound was loud and strong.
passages.original: אָ֥ז הָלְמ֖וּ עִקְּבֵי־ ס֑וּס מִֽדַּהֲר֖וֹת דַּהֲר֥וֹת אַבִּירָֽיו׃

passages.text: ‘Curse Meroz,’ says the angel of the LORD. ‘Bitterly curse her inhabitants; for they did not come to help the LORD, to help the LORD against the mighty.’
passages.sermon:
The angel of the LORD spoke.
The angel said, “Curse Meroz.”
Curse the people who live in Meroz.
They did not come to help the LORD.
They did not come to help the LORD fight against the strong enemies.
passages.original: א֣וֹרוּ מֵר֗וֹז אָמַר֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה אֹ֥רוּ אָר֖וֹר יֹשְׁבֶ֑יהָ כִּ֤י לֹֽא־ בָ֙אוּ֙ לְעֶזְרַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה לְעֶזְרַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה בַּגִּבּוֹרִֽים׃

passages.text: Most blessed among women is Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, most blessed of tent-dwelling women.
passages.sermon:
Jael was the wife of Heber the Kenite.
She lived in a tent.
Jael was a woman.
She was more blessed than other women.
She was the most blessed among women who live in tents.
passages.original: תְּבֹרַךְ֙ מִנָּשִׁ֔ים יָעֵ֕ל אֵ֖שֶׁת חֶ֣בֶר הַקֵּינִ֑י מִנָּשִׁ֥ים בָּאֹ֖הֶל תְּבֹרָֽךְ׃

passages.text: He asked for water, and she gave him milk. In a magnificent bowl she brought him curds.
passages.sermon: Sisera asked for water.\r\nJael gave him milk.\r\nShe brought him curds in a magnificent bowl.
passages.original: מַ֥יִם שָׁאַ֖ל חָלָ֣ב נָתָ֑נָה בְּסֵ֥פֶל אַדִּירִ֖ים הִקְרִ֥יבָה חֶמְאָֽה׃

passages.text: She reached for the tent peg, her right hand for the workman’s hammer. She struck Sisera and crushed his skull; she shattered and pierced his temple.
passages.sermon:
Jael was the wife of Heber the Kenite.
She acted with courage and strength.
She reached for the tent peg with her hand.
She took the workman’s hammer in her right hand.
She struck Sisera with the hammer.
She crushed Sisera’s skull.
She shattered his temple.
She pierced his temple.
passages.original: יָדָהּ֙ לַיָּתֵ֣ד תִּשְׁלַ֔חְנָה וִֽימִינָ֖הּ לְהַלְמ֣וּת עֲמֵלִ֑ים וְהָלְמָ֤ה סִֽיסְרָא֙ מָחֲקָ֣ה רֹאשׁ֔וֹ וּמָחֲצָ֥ה וְחָלְפָ֖ה רַקָּתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: At her feet he collapsed, he fell, there he lay still; at her feet he collapsed, he fell; where he collapsed, there he fell dead.
passages.sermon:
Sisera was a commander of Israel’s enemies.
Jael was a woman who killed Sisera.
Sisera came to Jael’s tent.
Jael struck Sisera and killed him.
Sisera fell at Jael’s feet.
He collapsed.
He lay still.
Sisera fell at Jael’s feet.
He collapsed.
Where Sisera collapsed, he died.
passages.original: בֵּ֣ין רַגְלֶ֔יהָ כָּרַ֥ע נָפַ֖ל שָׁכָ֑ב בֵּ֤ין רַגְלֶ֙יהָ֙ כָּרַ֣ע נָפָ֔ל בַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּרַ֔ע שָׁ֖ם נָפַ֥ל שָׁדֽוּד׃

passages.text: Sisera’s mother looked through the window; she peered through the lattice and lamented: ‘Why is his chariot so long in coming? What has delayed the clatter of his chariots?’
passages.sermon:
Sisera was a commander of the Canaanite army.
His mother waited for him to return from battle.
Sisera’s mother looked through the window.
She peered through the lattice.
She cried out in sorrow.
She said, “Why is his chariot taking so long to come?”
She asked, “What has delayed the sound of his chariots?”
passages.original: בְּעַד֩ הַחַלּ֨וֹן נִשְׁקְפָ֧ה וַתְּיַבֵּ֛ב אֵ֥ם סִֽיסְרָ֖א בְּעַ֣ד הָֽאֶשְׁנָ֑ב מַדּ֗וּעַ בֹּשֵׁ֤שׁ רִכְבּוֹ֙ לָב֔וֹא מַדּ֣וּעַ אֶֽחֱר֔וּ פַּעֲמֵ֖י מַרְכְּבוֹתָֽיו׃

passages.text: Her wisest ladies answer; indeed she keeps telling herself, ‘Are they not finding and dividing the spoil— a girl or two for each warrior, a plunder of dyed garments for Sisera, the spoil of embroidered garments for the neck of the looter?’
passages.sermon:
Sisera’s mother stands at the window.
She wonders about her son.
Her wisest ladies speak to her.
They try to comfort her.
She also answers herself.
She says, “They are finding and dividing the spoil.
Each warrior takes a girl or two.
Sisera receives plunder of dyed garments.
He takes embroidered cloth as spoil.
The looter puts the embroidered cloth around his neck.”
passages.original: חַכְמ֥וֹת שָׂרוֹתֶ֖יהָ תַּעֲנֶ֑ינָּה אַף־ הִ֕יא תָּשִׁ֥יב אֲמָרֶ֖יהָ לָֽהּ׃ הֲלֹ֨א יִמְצְא֜וּ יְחַלְּק֣וּ שָׁלָ֗ל רַ֤חַם רַחֲמָתַ֙יִם֙ לְרֹ֣אשׁ גֶּ֔בֶר שְׁלַ֤ל צְבָעִים֙ לְסִ֣יסְרָ֔א שְׁלַ֥ל צְבָעִ֖ים רִקְמָ֑ה צֶ֥בַע רִקְמָתַ֖יִם לְצַוְּארֵ֥י שָׁלָֽל׃

passages.text: So may all your enemies perish, O LORD! But may those who love You shine like the sun at its brightest.” And the land had rest for forty years.
passages.sermon:
The Lord has enemies.
May all Your enemies perish, O Lord.
The Lord also has people who love Him.
May those who love You shine.
They will shine like the sun at its brightest.
The land had peace for forty years.
